title: Display the current date and time in the terminal
summary: Show the current date and time in your Terminal. You can choose a standard format, a universal ISO format, or a numeric timestamp.

steps.explain: Display the current date and time using the default format for your region.
steps.expect: The current date and time, e.g., 'Mon Oct 23 10:30:00 AM 2023'.

steps.explain: Display the current date and time in UTC using the ISO 8601 format, which is standard for logs and programming.

alternatives.explain: Display the current time as a Unix timestamp (seconds since Jan 1, 1970).
alternatives.expect: A large number representing the current time, e.g., '1698071400'.

steps.explain: Convert a specific Unix timestamp into a readable date and time.

placeholders.name: UNIX_TIMESTAMP
placeholders.description: The Unix timestamp (seconds since epoch) you want to convert.

steps.expect: The readable date corresponding to the timestamp.

steps.explain: Calculate and display a date relative to the current time (e.g., 1 day forward, 20 minutes back).

placeholders.name: OFFSET
placeholders.description: Time offset, e.g., '+1d' for 1 day forward, '-20m' for 20 minutes back.

steps.expect: The calculated future or past date.
